'''Sheila D. Minor''' (born {{birth based on age as of date |71 |2018|03|19}}<ref name="nytimes" />), formerly '''Sheila Jones''' (now '''Sheila Minor Huff'''), is a former Biological Research Technician whose 35-year career included positions at the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]], the [[Department of the Interior]], and the [[Smithsonian Institution]].<ref name="CTV news">{{cite web|last1=Lagerquist|first1=Jeff|title=Twitter helps solve decades-old mystery of lone black woman pictured among male scientists|url=https://www.ctvnews.ca/sci-tech/article/twitter-helps-solve-decades-old-mystery-of-lone-black-woman-pictured-among-male-scientists/|website=[[CTV News Channel (Canada)]]|access-date=18 March 2018 |language=en-CA|date=16 March 2018}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Minor earned her bachelor's degree in [[Biological Sciences|biological sciences]] and worked for Clyde Jones at the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|last1=Mansky|first1=Jackie|title=How Smithsonian Helped Solve the Twitter Mystery of the Unknown Woman Scientist|url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smithsonian-institution/how-Smithsonian-helped-solve-mystery-unknown-female-scientist-1971-photo-180968518/|publisher=[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian]] |accessdate=18 March 2018|language=en}}</ref> When Minor applied for her first job, at the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, the company insisted she had to be a secretary. Knowing the worth of her knowledge, Minor didn't take that position.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fortin|title=She was the Only Woman in a Photo of 38 Scientists, and Now She's Been Identified|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/19/us/twitter-mystery-photo.html|accessdate=30 March 2018|agency=New York Times}}</ref>

She spent two years researching the mammals of [[Poplar Island (Chesapeake Bay)|Poplar Island]], and presented this work at the [[American Society of Mammalogists]] meeting in 1975. She earned a master's degree in environmental science at [[George Mason University]] and worked with K-12 schools on science education.<ref name=":0" />

She ran a Department of Interior office in Chicago.<ref name=":3" />

Minor served on the Smithsonian Women's Council.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.whimn.com.au/talk/news/why-theres-a-quest-to-uncover-who-this-mystery-woman-is/news-story/7e6e2db09e0db203c74de92a37145968|title=Why There's A Quest To Uncover Who This 'Mystery Woman' Is|work=whimn|access-date=2018-03-18}}</ref> She had a 35-year-long career at various federal bureaus including the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XTY3AQAAMAAJ&q=sheila+huff+environmental+protection+specialist&pg=SA4-PA49-IA30|title=Internal Revenue Service Facility, Detroit: Environmental Impact Statement|date=1991|language=en}}</ref> where she was responsible for assessing [[environmental impact statement]]s for many projects, ranging from [[hydroelectric dams]] to [[noise abatement]] procedures.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MeM3AQAAMAAJ&q=Sheila+Minor+Huff&pg=PA105|title=VA National Cemetery, Northeastern Illinois: Environmental Impact Statement|date=1991|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9-M0AQAAMAAJ&q=Sheila+Minor+environment&pg=SL3-PA26|title=US 61, US 218 and IA-394 Highway Improvements, Lewis County, Clark County [MO], Lee County, Henry County [IA]: Environmental Impact Statement|date=1999|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ROQ3AQAAMAAJ&q=Sheila+Minor+environment&pg=PA129|title=Cleveland National Cemetery: Environmental Impact Statement|date=1992|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9OM0AQAAMAAJ&q=sheila+minor+huff&pg=SA1-PA70|title=Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport, Air Traffic Control Noise Abatement Procedures: Environmental Impact Statement|date=1992|language=en}}</ref> At retirement in 2006,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/03/20/health/woman-scientist-1971-twitter-mystery-trnd/index.html|title=The identity of the lone woman scientist in this 1971 photo was a mystery. Then Twitter cracked the case|first=David |last=Williams|work=CNN|access-date=2018-03-23}}</ref> Minor was a senior employee in the Department of the Interior.<ref name="nytimes">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/19/us/twitter-mystery-photo.html|title=She Was the Only Woman in a Photo of 38 Scientists, and Now She's Been Identified |first=Jacey |last=Fortin |date=19 March 2018 |work=[[New York Times]] }}</ref>

As of 2018, Huff lives in Virginia,<ref name="nytimes" /> where she is an active member of her church and belly dances for a hobby.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theroot.com/meet-the-trailblazing-black-scientist-twitter-helped-id-1823930813|title=Meet the Trailblazing Black Scientist Twitter Helped Identify From a Single Photograph: Report|last=Branigin|first=Anne|work=The Root|access-date=2018-07-05|language=en-US}}</ref>

== International Conference on the Biology of Whales ==
Minor's story became a matter of public interest in 2018, when a photograph of conference attendees appeared on [[Twitter]]. Sheila Minor was the only woman in the conference's group photo, and the only person labelled as 'not identified'.  Candace Jean Anderson, an artist and writer from [[Salt Lake City, Utah]], came across the photograph whilst researching a picture book on the [[Marine Mammal Protection Act]].<ref name=":0" /> She took to Twitter to find out who the unidentified woman was, and the tweet went viral.<ref name=":0" />  
Eventually over 11,000 people answered her initial call for help, including the [[Smithsonian Institution]]'s Deborah Shapiro.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |first=Cindy |last=Arboleda|url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/twitter-found-name-history-trailblazing-black-woman-science-field-184702802.html|title=Twitter found the name and history of this trailblazing black female scientist|access-date=2018-03-18 |publisher=[[Yahoo! News]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |first=Hector |last=Llanos Martínez |url=https://verne.elpais.com/verne/2018/03/17/articulo/1521297535_391728.html|title=El misterio de Sheila Minor, la única mujer entre hombres en una conferencia científica de 1971|trans-title=The mystery of Sheila Minor, the sole woman among men at a 1971 scientific conference |date=2018-03-17|newspaper=[[El País]] |access-date=2018-03-18|language=es}}</ref> Anderson reached out to Minor on Facebook and the two spoke for a few hours.<ref name=":3" />

The photograph was taken at the 1971 International Conference on the Biology of Whales.  The conference was attended by almost 40 international scientists and conservationists, and co-organised by [[Matilene Berryman]] and [[Suzanne Montgomery Contos]], who were also uncovered in the Twitter conversation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wendybrandes.com/blog/2018/03/sheila-d-minor-a-hidden-figure-found-on-twitter/  |title=A Hidden Figure, Identified {{!}} Wendy Brandes Jewelry Blog|website=www.wendybrandes.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-18}}</ref> The photograph was taken by [[G. Carleton Ray]], who remembered Minor by name but had assumed she was an assistant administrator.<ref name=":0" /> 
The story of the "mystery whale scientist" was covered extensively in the media.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newsweek.com/twitter-sleuths-identify-mystery-whale-scientist-unnamed-woman-1971-conference-849380|title=Twitter sleuths identify mystery whale scientist, unnamed woman in 1971 conference photograph|date=2018-03-17|newspaper=[[Newsweek]] |access-date=2018-03-18|language=en}}</ref><ref name="CTV news" /><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thelily.com/history-had-forgotten-this-female-scientist-then-a-social-media-army-found-her/|title=History had forgotten this female scientist. Then a social media army found her. - The Lily|last=Castillo|first=Monica|work=The Lily|access-date=2018-03-18|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> Minor's story has drawn comparisons between her and the women in [[Margot Lee Shetterly]]'s ''[[Hidden Figures]]''.<ref name=":1" />

== Personal life ==
Minor lives in Virginia and has five grandchildren.<ref name="nytimes" />
